title: Kubernetes: How Traffic Reaches Your Pods

scenes.line1: How does traffic reach your app?
scenes.say: Ever wondered how a request from the internet actually finds your container inside a Kubernetes cluster?

scenes.label: Pod
scenes.sub: One or more containers, same IP, same storage
scenes.say: First, your code runs inside a pod. That's the smallest unit in Kubernetes, wrapping one or more containers.

scenes.label: Service
scenes.sub: Stable IP and DNS in front of pods
scenes.say: But pods come and go. So a Service gives your app a stable address, always pointing to the right pods.

scenes.label: Ingress
scenes.sub: HTTP routing from outside the cluster
scenes.say: To handle web traffic from outside, Ingress routes requests by host or path to the right Service, with TLS if you need it.
Here’s the real path: DNS points to a cloud load balancer, which forwards to your ingress controller. Ingress picks the Service, which sends traffic to a ready pod.

scenes.question: Service exists, but no traffic. Why?
scenes.right: The Service selector doesn't match any pod labels, or pods aren't ready.
scenes.say: Interview trap: If your Service exists but traffic doesn’t reach pods, don’t blame the Service first. Check if its selector matches the pod labels, and if the pods are actually ready.
